subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 21, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 21, 2026. Welcome to today's snapshot of our progress and community happenings.  
Over the past few days our team has merged several intelligence sync commits that bring the latest newsletter, archive, and wiki guides into the repository. We also adjusted the CI pipeline in the immutable branch, passing -R to gh release create and fixing a YAML indentation issue that was blocking workflow validation. Additionally, the missing firefox-ublock-origin package was added to the Xlibre spin, and a GitLab mirror deploy key was refreshed to keep our downstream builds in sync.  
Darren has been fine‑tuning Calamares to ensure a smooth first‑boot experience, while Natalie continues to polish the Cinnamon desktop and XLibre themes. Recent work includes updated kernel configurations for better hardware compatibility and ongoing efforts to harden the distribution’s privacy profile. Meanwhile, the Fluorite browser received its latest ad‑blocking and privacy enhancements, building on the Chromium base with extra tracker protection.  
In the wider Arch ecosystem, a recent How‑To Geek feature highlighted how CachyOS eases the Arch learning curve, offering inspiration for our own documentation efforts. Sadly, a prominent Arch Linux developer announced their resignation after a decade of service, reminding us of the importance of maintaining healthy contributor turnover.  
Security concerns have also surfaced, with over four hundred AUR packages reportedly hijacked to spread infostealers and eBPF rootkits, prompting Arch to suspend new AUR registrations temporarily. On a brighter note, the Linux kernel prepatch 7.3‑rc4 is now available for testing, and Systemtap 5.6 has been released, offering improved tracing capabilities for developers and administrators.  
If you are installing AcreetionOS for the first time, remember to verify the ISO’s SHA256 checksum before flashing it to a USB drive. Our AcreetionMediaWriter tool works on Windows, macOS, and Linux, making the write process simple and reliable across platforms.  
Take advantage of the built‑in privacy browsers: Fluorite, a Chromium fork with aggressive ad blocking, and Cryolite, a GNU IceCat‑based Firefox derivative that emphasizes free‑software principles. Both are pre‑configured to block trackers and resist fingerprinting, giving you a safer browsing experience out of the box.  
We encourage you to join our Discord server for real‑time chat, contribute to the wiki if you spot outdated information, and report any bugs via the GitHub issue tracker. Regular community meetings are held every other Thursday, and the next one will focus on upcoming ISO release planning.  
Thank you to Natalie, Darren, and all our volunteers for the continued dedication that keeps AcreetionOS lightweight, private, and user
